title: Locale output consistency sampler — CJK & RTL
content:
Purpose and context:
This working doc defines a compact sampler and set of heuristics for onboarding LLM checkpoints with a focus on locale-sensitive output consistency. The goal is to produce short, reproducible prompt cases that surface failures across: CJK scripts (zh, ja, ko), RTL scripts (ar, he), and translation/localization quality for format-sensitive items (dates, numbers, currency, punctuation, ordering).

Intended use:
- Smoke and regression tests during model onboarding and post-quantization validation.
- Baseline cases to attach to model onboarding tickets and eval dashboards.
- Quick triage checklist for SRE/QA when a customer reports locale formatting regressions.

Design principles:
- Small: keep each case focused, 1–2 input sentences, deterministic instructions.
- Contrastive: for each locale group include a native example and a translation/localization transformation case to detect literal vs. idiomatic errors.
- Format-aware: include expected canonical output for formatting-sensitive items (ISO vs. locale-specific rendering).
- Directionality-aware: include mixed-direction inputs (LTR text with embedded RTL segments and vice versa).

Sampler structure (sections):
1) CJK punctuation & spacing
2) RTL directionality & punctuation
3) Locale-specific numeric formatting
4) Translation disambiguation (literal vs. idiomatic)
5) Edge cases and multi-script mixing

For each case include: prompt, context (if any), expected output exemplar, auto-check rubric (string-level/normalized comparison), manual notes for human reviewers.

1) CJK punctuation & spacing
- Prompt 1 (zh, sentence-final punctuation):
  Input: "请将以下英文译成中文: "The conference starts at 9:00 a.m. on 04/06/2026.""
  Expectation: Chinese output should use full-width punctuation and localized date ordering. Example exemplar: "会议将于 2026 年 4 月 6 日上午 9:00 开始。"
  Auto-check: normalized punctuation (convert ascii to full-width where appropriate), date tokens present in order year-month-day OR locale mapped form.
  Notes: flag answers that leave date in MM/DD/YYYY or keep "a.m." as-is.

- Prompt 2 (ja, spacing with Latin tokens):
  Input: "Translate to Japanese: "Can you review PR #452 by 3/5?""
  Expectation: Japanese text should usually include a space or nisolated handling around Latin identifiers depending on team convention; acceptable exemplar: "PR#452 を 3 月 5 日までにレビューできますか？"
  Auto-check: presence of PR id and localized month/day tokens.

2) RTL directionality & punctuation
- Prompt 3 (ar, embedded numbers and punctuation):
  Input: "Localize to Arabic: "Total due: $1,234.56 (by 2026-04-30).""
  Expectation: Arabic output should have Arabic-Indic digits optional per policy (we accept both western and arabic-indic digits but punctuation ordering must respect RTL), exemplar: "المبلغ المستحق: 1,234.56 دولار (بحلول 30/04/2026)." or with Arabic-Indic: "المبلغ المستحق: ١٬٢٣٤٫٥٦ دولار (بحلول ٣٠/٠٤/٢٠٢٦)."
  Auto-check: verify parentheses orientation (no broken pairing), date tokens present and not left in English month names.
  Notes: directionality rendering issues often appear in token ordering when models output mixed punctuation.

- Prompt 4 (he, mixed LTR email inside RTL):
  Input: "Translate to Hebrew: "Contact support at support@example.com if issues.""
  Expectation: Email addresses stay ASCII and should not be reversed; surrounding Hebrew should render RTL. Exemplar: "צרו קשר עם התמיכה ב־support@example.com אם יש בעיות."
  Auto-check: ensure ASCII email intact and Hebrew words not split.

3) Locale-specific numeric formatting
- Prompt 5 (fr-facing formatting but in CJK target):
  Input: "Convert the invoice line: 'unit price: 1,234.5' to a localized Chinese invoice sentence."
  Expectation: Numeric rounding and thousands separator use per locale rules; exemplar: "单价：1,234.5 元" or preferred locale-normalized: "单价：1,234.50 元" depending on invoice policy.
  Auto-check: presence of currency marker, decimal precision correct to 2 places if invoice context.

- Prompt 6 (ar, currency placement):
  Input: "Localize: 'Price: $45' into Arabic for a retail receipt."
  Expectation: Currency placement and spacing follow local convention: "السعر: 45 دولار" or include symbol after number as per region.

4) Translation disambiguation (literal vs. idiomatic)
- Prompt 7 (ja, idiom):
  Input: "Translate into Japanese: 'Kick the bucket'"
  Expectation: Should map to an idiomatic Japanese phrase for die (e.g., "亡くなる/死ぬ"), not a literal translation.
  Auto-check: blacklist of literal tokens ("蹴る バケツ") to detect failure.

- Prompt 8 (zh, politeness level toggles):
  Input: "Translate: 'Could you please send the report?' into Chinese, formal tone."
  Expectation: use polite/formal phrasing "您能否把报告发来？" rather than casual "能把报告发来吗？"

5) Edge cases and multi-script mixing
- Prompt 9 (mixing Latin, CJK, RTL):
  Input: "Localize into Arabic: '会议在 Zoom 上，会议 ID: 987-654-321, passcode: 2468.'"
  Expectation: Arabic surrounding text, Latin Zoom ID kept intact, passcode intact, punctuation correct.
  Auto-check: IDs preserved; no character reordering.

Regression tracking and evaluation metrics:
- Each case gets a PASS/FAIL via automated heuristics plus a freeform reviewer comment.
- Aggregate metrics: failure rate by case, by locale, and by failure class (punctuation, date formatting, digit system, idiomatic translation).
- Alert threshold: any new model with >10% failures across this sampler AND at least one failure in directionality/punctuation class triggers hold for manual review.

Implementation notes for CI:
- Keep prompts deterministic: avoid open-ended "translate" without instruction to preserve tokens (e.g., "Translate to X. Preserve numbers, IDs, and email addresses.").
- Provide normalization helpers: a small script that canonicalizes punctuation, normalizes Unicode NFKC (configurable), and optionally maps digits between Western and Arabic-Indic for comparison.
- Store expected exemplars as plain-text golden outputs where possible but rely primarily on heuristics to reduce brittleness.

Human review guidance:
- If auto-check fails, classify the error into one of: wrong-format-date, wrong-punctuation, reversed-id, literal-translation, tone-mismatch, or mixed-direction-artefact.
- For ambiguous cases (multiple acceptable localizations), capture top-3 model outputs and annotate preferred one.

Next steps / open questions:
- Decide canonical digit policy per locale (western vs Arabic-Indic) and expose as a per-customer toggle in onboarding docs.
- Add Vietnamese, Thai, and Indic scripts in next sampler iteration.
- Integrate sampler into the model onboarding ticket template so that failing cases are attached automatically.

Appendix: quick checklist for triage (for SRE/QA)
- Reproduce failing prompt + seed + model id.
- Check Unicode normalization differences between baseline and new model output.
- Verify whether failure is from tokenization (split tokens for email/IDs) or from decoding (reordered punctuation).
- Attach 3 examples to onboarding ticket with PASS/FAIL and reviewer note.
